entities.summary: Nicomachus of Gerasa, a 2nd-century CE Neopythagorean philosopher, played a significant role in shaping the mathematical and musical thought of the Roman period. Born in Arabia Petraea, Nicomachus wrote extensively on the mystical properties of numbers, which became a standard text for Neoplatonic education. His works, including the "Introduction to Arithmetic" and the "Manual of Harmonics", demonstrate a deep understanding of Ancient Greek mathematics and music theory. As a key figure in the Neopythagorean movement, Nicomachus contributed to the development of mathematical and musical knowledge in the Roman Empire. His ideas influenced prominent figures of the time, including Emperor Hadrian and the Roman poet, Ausonius. Nicomachus' legacy can be seen in the transmission of mathematical and musical knowledge from Ancient Greece to the Renaissance era, with his works surviving in manuscripts from the 12th to the 19th centuries. The exact date of his birth remains unknown, but his writings provide valuable insights into the mathematical and musical thought of the 2nd century CE. Despite the passage of time, Nicomachus' contributions to the development of mathematical and musical knowledge continue to be studied and appreciated by scholars today.
